chunks: Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad al-Razi narrated to me, saying: Ali ibn Muhammad al-Hurmuzani narrated to us, from Abu Abdillah al-Husayn ibn Ali عليه السلام, who said:

When Fatimah عليها السلام passed away, Amir al-Mu'minin buried her secretly and effaced the place of her grave. Then he stood, turned his face toward the grave of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, and said: Peace be upon you, O Messenger of Allah, from me, and peace be upon you from your daughter, your visitor, the one spending the night in the earth at your spot, for whom Allah chose swift joining with you.

O Messenger of Allah, my patience has become little over your chosen one, and my endurance has faded over the chief of the women of the worlds, except that in taking consolation through your sunnah in your separation there is for me a place of solace. I indeed laid you in the niche of your grave, and your soul flowed forth between my throat and my chest.
Yes; and in the Book of Allah there is for me the best acceptance: “Indeed we belong to Allah, and indeed to Him we are returning.”

The trust has been taken back, the pledge has been seized, and al-Zahra has been taken away. How ugly the green earth and the dusty land have become, O Messenger of Allah. As for my grief, it is everlasting; and as for my night, it is sleepless; and sorrow will not depart from my heart until Allah chooses for me your abode in which you reside.

A festering anguish and a stirring sorrow—how quickly separation came between us. To Allah I complain, and your daughter will inform you of your community’s united oppression against her; so ask her insistently, and inquire from her about the condition. How much burning grief churned within her chest for which she found no way to disclose; and she will say: Allah judges, and He is the best of judges.

This is the farewell of one departing, not one displeased nor wearied. If I leave, it is not from weariness; and if I remain, it is not from سوء ظنّ toward what Allah has promised the patient. Ah, ah—patience is more blessed and more beautiful. Were it not for the domination of those who seized control, I would have made remaining and staying here an inseparable commitment, and I would have wailed like a bereaved mother over the tremendous calamity. Thus, before the sight of Allah, your daughter is buried secretly, her right is usurped, her inheritance is withheld, though the عهد has not grown distant and the remembrance of you has not faded. To Allah, O Messenger of Allah, is the complaint; and in you, O Messenger of Allah, is the finest consolation. May Allah send blessings upon you, and upon her be peace and good pleasure.

key_terms.إِرْثَهَا: Her inheritance that was withheld from her.
key_terms.الزَّهْرَاءُ: A title of Fatimah عليها السلام, referring here to her being taken away in death.
key_terms.الْمُسْتَوْلِينَ: Those who seized control or gained domination.
key_terms.الْمُشْتَكَى: The complaint that is directed to Allah.
key_terms.الْوَدِيعَةُ: The entrusted deposit returned to Allah, referring to Fatimah عليها السلام.
key_terms.تَجَلُّدِي: My endurance or outward composure in the face of grief.
key_terms.هَضْمِهَا: The diminishing and usurpation of her rights.

ai.seo_question: What did أمير المؤمنين عليه السلام say after the burial of Fatimah عليها السلام?
ai.summary: This narration recounts the burial of Fatimah عليها السلام in secrecy and the address of أمير المؤمنين عليه السلام to the grave of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله. It expresses grief, patience, complaint to Allah, and the wrongs suffered by Fatimah عليها السلام, including the usurpation of her rights and inheritance.
